Row 49 was read directly with openpyxl from BOTH frozen XLSX files: Quality Checks row 50 and Internal Quality Checks row 50. The public wording requires every repeated runtime fact to agree; the Internal annotation does not narrow the shipped profile. Harbor quality-checks.md:196-198 and staged-task-contract.md:Cross-file agreements were applied.

CONFIRMED inherited runtime-contract conflict: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:23 says "Only S22 invokes restart_app, exactly once" and distinguishes a completed restart from a tool failure; :410 requires a completed process restart before fresh-page readback. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:350 says "The one process restart preserves" exact saved fields/revisions. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:15-19 advertises stopping and relaunching the application, and :47 returns "restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP" whenever the shell returns 0. However tests/test.sh:152-159 sends SIGTERM and waits at most 50 * 0.1 seconds without rejecting a surviving old process or forcibly terminating it. It then starts a new process (:160-169), accepts any HTTP listener on port 3000 (:130-145, :170-183), and exits 0. It does not establish that the old process stopped or the replacement owns the answering listener. Thus the helper's actual success condition contradicts the process-restart fact asserted by its MCP wrapper and consumed by S22.

Raw runtime verification: independently checked the SHA256 of qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-repair3/inherited-restart-counterexample.json against raw-evidence-index.json, checked its template_test_sha256 against the frozen tests/test.sh, and extracted the exact current heredoc to verify helper_original_sha256. All match. Read qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-09-30/reproduce_restart.py:7-26: its minimal source deliberately retains the old process on SIGTERM, identifies each actual answering PID, and invokes the extracted unchanged helper. The raw JSON records helper_returncode=0, old_pid=7, claimed_new_pid=67, old_still_running=true, and both before.pid and after.pid=7; restart_log contains EADDRINUSE for the replacement yet "app-restart pid=67 ready=1". This demonstrates incorrect restart-success semantics, not merely a heuristic concern. No new Docker/provider/network run was performed. Current tests/test.sh, restart_mcp.py and score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template, so this is an inherited conflict that requires a template-owner correction; task authors must not patch shared files silently.

Other repeated facts checked and consistent: integration.md:5 requires node /app/server.js, /app/public/index.html, 0.0.0.0:3000 and GET /api/health; tests/test.sh:48, :97-111, :136, :160-167, all five prompt opening URLs, app_context.md:4, server.js:12/:101-113 and solve.sh:4-7/:26 agree. DB_PATH/default /app/app.db agree between integration.md:7, test.sh:98-109/:165/:189 and server.js:8; the copy fallback consistently substitutes the selected entry and database into the restart helper. Seed scope is /assets/seed_data.json in instruction.md:5 and integration.md:9, copied by environment/Dockerfile:15 and covered by task.toml:2. Its snippets=[] describes no supplied user records, while examples belong to the app; later gate-created records are explicitly preserved by app_context.md:24 and all scored prompts. No fixed date/clock is required. The five-second source/callback budget agrees in behaviour.md:9, security.md:5, app_context.md:18 and Functional S09/S36; the prompt openly allows scheduling overhead and does not demand a separate five seconds per callback. The source/public runner files and source/public stylesheet bytes match, and source/bundle watchdog and runner-host literals agree. No-account/shared-library statements agree in instruction.md:1, overview.md:7, policy.md:3, app_context.md:8, and prompts; no demo account login is demanded.

All five judge fallbacks parse as claude-code, matching task.toml:31; its model remains z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx at :32, with no conflicting per-dimension model. tests/test.sh:193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER, functional/judge.toml:18 consumes exactly that variable, and functional prompt requests the restart_app tool exactly once, matching restart_mcp.py:14/:29-32. scoring.toml parses to gates render=constraints=0.0, weights functional=.6/polish=.2/visual=.2, floor functional=.05; score.py:10/:28-48 reads that policy directly. Parsed criterion counts are render 1, constraints 1, functional 64, polish 7, visual 6. task.toml makes no numerical criterion-count claim. Functional prompt:9's 23 protocols matches 23 actual S headings; the six-phase plan has six entries. Error-line literals in functional/judge.toml:175/:196/:217/:238 agree with the exact S10-S13 source fixtures at prompt.md:266-340. Viewport 390 by 844 agrees in Polish and Visual.

Conforming alternatives considered: no-sign-in apps, arbitrary backend request schemas, case-sensitive trimmed titles, either initial theme, optional pending preview visibility, and a second local loopback preview hostname are consistently allowed in the brief and injected context/protocols. No mismatch on these was demonstrated. A legitimate server with a long graceful shutdown is also not prohibited by integration.md; the harness must verify replacement rather than assume SIGTERM caused it. Full configured LLM judge timing/results, Oracle and target-model evidence remain unmeasured; the raw scripted evidence does not establish those results. All task-relative citations in this evidence resolve beneath .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/.
counterexample: Measured helper witness: a port-3000 server installs process.on("SIGTERM",()=>{}); the canonical helper claims a successful new PID while the original PID remains the responder and the replacement fails EADDRINUSE. Extending that observed mechanism to a functioning saved-library UI backed only by process memory would preserve records across this alleged restart and could falsely earn S22 restart-durability credit; that full weak-app judge score is an inference and was not measured. A conforming SQLite app with a slow graceful shutdown exposes the same false-success claim even though its actual restart durability has not been tested.
suggested_fix: Have the shared-template owner make restart success require verified termination of the old process group and a live replacement serving the probe, with bounded escalation/error handling; then regenerate the frozen candidate and remeasure the restart scenarios without task-local shared-harness edits.
